segments.text:
Verſ. 11.
For with a ſtammering tongue, and with a ſtrāge language ſhall he ſpeake vnto this people.

WHereas ſome ſupply, that it is as if one ſpake, it is ſuperfluous. I referre this to God then, who, as the Prophet ſaith, ſpake in a ſtrange language to this barbarous people. This reprehenſion ought therefore to haue pierced them to the heart, in regard that by their owne default they made him to ſlut and ſtammer, who yet giues ſpeech vnto all. He threatens them not, but rather accuſeth them of blockiſhnes, in that they made the heauenlie doctrine to become nothing elſe but a confuſed ſound vnto them, ſo as they receiued no benefit by it, becauſe they wittinglie ſtopped their eares againſt it. The Prophet therefore compares their follie to a thing againſt nature, in that they would not heare the voice of the Lord.
